answer: Joint attestation needs a kernel seal for every pair, recorded in the canyon ledger; each agent locks 60 credits. A seal costs 5 credits and binds two keys, the action id, and the comet tick: one seal per pair per action. For k fakes, pairs number k(k-1)/2; the kth fake adds k-1 seals costing 5(k-1), so the thousandth costs 4,995. A thousand fakes pay 2,497,500 plus 60,000 in bonds. A rented seal mismatches keys, tick, or action and burns the bond. Auditors recount canyon pairs at each comet tick and void incomplete actions. A lone honest agent needs no pair seal, only one refundable bond.
